title: Kargil political and social groups hold shutdown over winter election timing
seoTitle: Kargil shutdown over winter election timing

tea.why: Groups oppose holding Hill Council elections in December, citing that harsh winter weather causes mass migration and limits voter participation.
tea.want: The deferment of the Hill Council elections until after the winter season.
tea.changed: Nov 10: The Ladakh administration announced that Hill Council elections will proceed on December 4 despite the ongoing protest.

summary: On November 10, 2026, political parties and social organisations in Kargil observed a complete shutdown to protest the administration's decision to hold Hill Council elections during the winter. Organised by the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) and supported by local political and religious leaders, the protest aimed to highlight that 20% to 25% of the population, including students and the elderly, migrates during the harsh winter months. Leaders argued that winter polls would disenfranchise voters and hinder democratic participation due to difficult terrain and connectivity issues. On the same day, Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra announced that elections for 100 constituencies across eight districts would be held on December 4. The administration stated that the election process would conclude by December 8, maintaining that the councils would retain their existing legal powers.
demands: Postponement of polls until after winter
response: Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra announced that the elections will proceed on December 4, noting that the process will be completed by December 8 and that the councils will retain their existing powers.

updates.text: Political and social groups in Kargil announced a planned shutdown and candlelight march to protest potential winter election dates.
A shutdown was observed in Kargil as the administration officially announced that Hill Council elections would take place on December 4.
